name: Nested Molecular Hierarchy
description: Fig 8b — molecular compositions as a nested hierarchical composite. Molecular structure is organized as a nested place-graph across scales: an extracellular matrix, a membrane, and a cytoplasm containing a nucleus (chromosome → chromatin → nucleosome → DNA/histone), organelles (a ribosomal complex, mitochondria, secretory organelles), and cytoplasmic pools (proteins, RNA, enzymes, metabolites, nutrients). Six DRAFT processes act on leaves deep inside this hierarchy — transmembrane transport across the membrane, replication/repair and transcription in the nucleus, metabolism and translation in the cytoplasm, and assembly of subunits into the ribosomal complex — so the topology reads like Fig 8b. All DRAFT processes: unit-bearing ports + behavior contracts, no dynamics.
